spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
:
 The Dragon
 with Fourteen Heads

---


**
¶1:** What
 is
 handed
 down among
 those
 who possess external knowledge without
 interior
 understanding is
 this
: that
 there exists
 within
 the natural person a ruling
 love
 of self,
 poss
essing fourteen
 fac
ulties of out
ward perception,
 and that
 it
 lies
 concealed within
 five
 interior
 seats of the
 will
. But
 what truly
 is this
 ruling
 love of self with
 its fourteen modes of engaging
 the
 world?
 Is
 it something
 belonging
 to the body
 alone
 —
 or
 is it a teaching
 concerning
 spiritual states?

**¶2
:** There has
 never been a ruling
 love
 of self belonging
 merely
 to the flesh
 with
 fourteen out
ward powers
, as those
 who possess only
 external knowledge suppose
. Rather, this is a teaching about
 the
 spiritual life
 of
 the person
. It was first
 given
 in the
 purity of unc
orrupted doctrine, but
 those
 poss
essing external knowledge alone
 did not penet
rate to
 the interior
 meaning conce
aled within all
 their own
 transmitted
 words,
 which
 are throughout
 spiritual.


**¶3:** Now
 this
 is
 how it
 is to be
 understood: the natural person —
 the whole
 external
 self oriented
 toward the
 world — is itself
 what
 is sign
ified by this
 ruling
 self
-love. The doctrine
 of the flesh —
 the governing
 principle
 that
 the
 body
 and
 its desires
 are
 life
 itself — this
 is the dragon
.
 And
 the fourteen fac
ulties of out
ward perception distributed
 throughout
 it
 are as
 follows.


**¶4:** The seven
 modes
 of perception belonging
 to the understanding —
 the
 higher region
 of the
 mind — are these: the
 two
 fac
ulties of intellectual
 sight, by
 which one perce
ives ideas
 and
 forms; the two fac
ulties of reception
,
 by which one app
rehends tru
ths and fals
ities spoken
 from
 without
; the two faculties of interior
 disc
ernment, by which one perce
ives the quality and
 character
 of what
 approaches
;
 and
 also
 the faculty
 of discrimin
ating taste
, by which one sel
ects among
 the various
 kinds
 of good
 and evil that
 present
 themselves in
 every
 out
ward form.

**¶5
:** These are the seven powers
 of the ruling
 self-love belonging
 to the understanding —
 the seven
 modes
 of out
ward perception that
 r
eside in the higher
 region
 of the person
's
 mind.
 And
 below
 these,
 corresponding
 to each
, are seven
 appet
ites of the will:
 the c
ravings and
 impul
ses that
 answer
 to every
 faculty
 of perception above
.
 Just
 as the seven faculties of understanding
 se
ize upon the world
 from
 above, so seven
 corresponding
 desires
 of the will gra
sp at it
 from below.
 Together they complete
 the
 fourteen powers
 through
 which self
-love gov
erns the whole natural
 person.

**¶6:**
 Now
 the
 five interior
 seats in
 which this
 self
-love lies
 concealed,
 from
 which it emerges and through
 which it acts
,
 are these: The
 first
 is the faculty
 of speech
 and
 expression — for
 through utter
ance,
 self
-love first
 projects
 itself into
 the world.
 The second is the faculty of thought —
 the
 resp
iration of the natural
 mind
,
 through
 which self
-love sust
ains its
 life in
 reasoning
 and
 persu
asion. The third is the will
 itself
 — the in
most
 love
 from
 which all intention
 flows
. The fourth is the faculty by
 which di
sor
dered affections are processed
 and
 retained
 rather
 than pur
ified. The fifth is the vital
 force itself — the anim
ating current
 that flows
 through all the
 rest
,
 carrying
 self
-love into
 every
 part
 of the person
's
 life
.
 When this ruling
 self-love emerges from
 these
 five interior seats and
 manif
ests its
 lik
eness and its
 vigil
ance through
 both
 understanding
 and will, it wages spiritual war by
 means
 of all
 fourteen faculties of
 out
ward perception at
 once.

**¶8
:** Thus
 it
 has
 been set
 forth:
 the ruling
 love
 of self that
 dw
ells within
 the natural person, poss
essing fourteen modes of outward perception and
 five interior seats of the
 will in
 which it lies
 concealed and
 hidden. Through
 these it exercises its desire
 contin
ually —
 for
 self
-love never
 r
ests,
 but perpet
ually seeks
 domin
ion through
 every
 faculty it
 inhab
its.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: They say that there is a dragon with fourteen heads, and it is gathered in and [hidden in its] den with five refuges. What really is a corporeal dragon with fourteen heads? Or is it another spiritual lesson?

There is never a dragon in the flesh with fourteen heads, as the Magi say! Rather, this is a spiritual lesson. It was uttered in virginity [of pure doctrine, but] the Magi did not understand [the interior meaning concealed within] all their words that are written [, which are wholly spiri]tual (?).

Again, this is how this earth [of the body is, and what belongs] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [, the whole of the natural person.] I will instruct you [concerning this:] the Dragon is this doctrine [and ruling principle] of the flesh [and its desires;] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the Dragon are these.

The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [, which is the one of taste,] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.

These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [and seven are] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [hands]; the two [of the feet; the belly, the] ruler [of desire; and the organ of generation and of excretion. As are] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.

Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the Dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and manifest its likeness and its vigilance above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.

Whoever will recognise them with the dragon, which is the thought of the body, and struggles with it and is victorious and kills it in them He receives the victory without suffering on the day of his coming forth.
the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [all that it wills, pursuing its des]ire all the time.
